lighter_prose.passage: The kaleidoscope also matters as a *teaching instrument*. You can build one. This is critical in the context of the Four Pillars: the tool that demonstrates the philosophy is itself a tool you can make and modify. The Max/MSP patch that generates the visual identity — the Lissajous pattern in a sphere — is a kaleidoscope of sorts. Students don't just learn about prisms; they build the prism machine and watch it generate new patterns as they adjust parameters. The learning happens *through the making of the machine itself*.
lighter_prose.words: You can build a kaleidoscope, and students can: the patch that draws the Lissajous-in-a-sphere identity is one, and changing its parameters teaches what a prism does. (This repeats the Visual Identity section's 'Students can download it, modify it'; keep one.)

lighter_prose.passage: The question was: are they truly separate domains that need to be integrated, or are they always-already unified and we're just perceiving them as separate? The prism metaphor resolved this: they're unified in the higher dimension. Our perception separates them. The light of curiosity is what creates the projection.
lighter_prose.words: The pillars are not separate domains to be integrated; they are one thing, and our perception separates them. The light of curiosity makes the projection. (The opening paragraph already says this.)

summary: Read the hub whole and all 16 source pages (the passages that speak of the hub plus each page's links block). Pattern: the genuine relations are of two kinds, the prism-machine instances (Wallpaper Groups, Crystal Synthesizer, both named as such on page and hub) and the one-thing-many-views echoes (Dispersion, Meaning and the Link, Autodidact Polymaths, Stoicism, Wavetable, Kuramoto); six links (Embeddings, Bessel, Slime Mold, Categorizing Inharmonicity, Action Potential, Quantum) have no sentence on either page that carries the hub's idea, and several lean on Spinoza's monism instead, which they already link. Verdicts: 4 label, 4 retype, 6 cut, 2 keep. Not settled: (1) the Kuramoto pair carries two links, since the hub holds its own bare connects-to back to Kuramoto; I kept the labelled side and suggest dropping the hub's, but that edit is outside this brief. (2) Whether the Founding Conversation is better typed spawned (as proposed) or left as a labelled connects-to. (3) The P5.js versus Max/MSP contradiction on the hub is Loudon's to settle. No newcomer entry had a genuine inbound link from these pages, so typed_relations is empty.
